why: VAMPIRES ARE THE FUEL, NOT THE ENGINE (the pilot, 2026-11-11): blood drain, life gain, action at a distance, ferocious; pings that snowball, never a two-card infinite; bracket 3. As of 2026-11-13 the branch is nineteen out, nineteen in against the sleeved v3.0.0, in five jobs. DRAIN ON EVERY DEATH: Zulaport Cutthroat, Elas il-Kor, Falkenrath Noble, Bastion of Remembrance and The Meathook Massacre drain each opponent, Teysa Karlov doubles them, Skullclamp draws off them. THE LOOP: Pitiless Plunderer + Ashnod's Altar with Oathsworn Vampire or Reassembling Skeleton and a drainer (stack 013); the burst turn with Teysa (stack 014); both checker-passed. REMOVAL WITH FANGS (log 008 and the pilot, 2026-11-13): Swords to Plowshares, Vanishing Verse, Crackling Doom (an edict through hexproof), Toxic Deluge (Olivia's Wrath killed the branch's own non-Vampire engines). PROTECTION THAT NEEDS NO COMMANDER: Boros Charm, Selfless Spirit, Giver of Runes replace Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver, which sat in hand until Edgar (six mana) was out; the pilot: protection is always needed against the A team. MANA: thirty-five lands (Sacred Foundry, a Plains) for the Talismans and Rakdos Signet. Wispdrinker Vampire stays (cut in iteration two, restored: an entering-token drain the pilot credited in log 008). Rejected 2026-11-13: Anowon (taxes the branch's own non-Vampires), Impact Tremors / Corpse Knight / Ayara (the pilot did not like the cuts), Dauntless Bodyguard (Selfless Spirit does it for the board). Forge A/B (iteration one, 200/arm, olivers-table-nov): no resolvable difference on life removed, removal cast doubled; the AI rarely assembles the loop.

Pilot approved 2026-11-20 (card 1 of the research pass): steady, board-independent draw that survives a wipe — the loss shape in logs 001/002/003/006 was a wipe then an empty hand by T8-10; every other draw source on the branch is on-plan (a death, a token entering). The Mercenary is a changeling Vampire: Elas gains, the gain drains, then fodder. Reaper draws only on nontoken deaths (the clause Haruspex was cut for) and is a non-Vampire body. Decided by deck-doctor + strategist; no goldfish figure used.

Card 2 (2026-11-20, pilot approved): the branch had no Vampire-count finisher after cutting Sanctum Seeker; Bloodwitch is the thesis in one card (drain, gain, action at a distance, scales with the fuel, pro-white flyer). Cordial's counters pay off only in combat and fight Skullclamp; stacks 002/009/010 named it and are now historical.

Card 3 (2026-11-20, pilot approved): the branch's second phase-out beside Teferi's Protection — the one shape that beats the sacrifice, -X/-X, bounce and exile wipes (a third of the 60 across the 22 opponent seats) that indestructible misses; convokes free off eminence tokens with every land tapped on Vampires (log 002), covers the noncreature engine, needs no Edgar. Akroma's Will is the redundant indestructible shape at four mana with an Edgar-gated combat finisher; Boros Charm kept (two mana, all permanents). Strategist dissented: would cut Boros Charm and keep the Will's lifelink alpha.

Card 4 (2026-11-20, pilot approved): removal was the thinnest axis left (four single-target instants plus two wipes); Scheme is the only removal candidate the eminence tokens cast for free at instant speed (log 002: no open mana), kills Krenko/Tannuk/Zur/every planeswalker across the seats, and connive is draw. Olivia's ping ({1}{R} per point) and steal ({3}{B}{B}) were the slowest, most mana-hungry removal and the hungriest red card on 13 sure red sources. Dissent (strategist): cut Boros Charm, keep Olivia; the pilot chose Olivia.

Card 5 (2026-11-20, pilot approved): restores the branch's only drain that converts board width — each attacking Vampire drains each opponent on declaration, blockers never see it (the pilot's own notes: 'drain from a distance, no combat needed', 'not an anthem at all'); 71% of B3 lists; un-strands passing stacks 001/003/005/007; its 2026-11-11 cut was a slot trade for Elas with no case against it. Noble is the eighth death-drainer and the lowest yield (four mana, one point, one target); Vampire for Vampire, four for four, no draw or stack lost. Alternative cut (strategist): Giver of Runes — kept under the protection rule.

Card 6 (2026-11-20, pilot approved; the doctor called it modest, the strategist would have stopped): the branch's nine draw cards are all one-per-event and it had no draw-X refuel, the shape of the losses in logs 001/002/003/006; log 001 names Champion in the pilot's own words. Beats Pact of the Serpent here: Master of Dark Rites' mana casts only Vampire spells, Urza's Incubator makes it three, eminence floors X at two post-wipe, Vampire for Vampire. Preacher yields a token OR a card per attack, the steady shape the branch has nine of.

summary.title: Vampires as fuel: drain every death, removal with fangs, draw, a finisher
summary.blurb: Turns Edgar's tokens into a drain engine (each-opponent death triggers, Teysa doubling them, a Plunderer and Altar loop, Skullclamp draw); adds edicts and a chosen-size wipe, protection that needs no commander, Black Market Connections for steady draw, Malakir Bloodwitch as the Vampire-count finisher, and more lands.
